page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.8-32 is a compute-focused instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration features 8 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8358 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. System memory is sized at 32.0 GB, which corresponds to 2.0 GB per vCPU (or 4.0 GB per physical core). Dedicated core allocation ensures that execution threads remain isolated from neighboring virtual machines.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, having 0 GPUs and no integrated NVMe volumes. Persistent operating system files and data volumes must be configured through remote block storage. For external networking and inbound access, the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this profile prioritizes computational capacity over memory density. It offers resource and cost efficiency for environments where oversized memory pools are unnecessary, avoiding expenditures on surplus RAM. Conversely, it is not structured for in-memory databases or data pipeline caching layers that demand larger memory allocations. The instance is suited for batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed microservices, and general CPU-bound application servers.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.8-32 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by an Intel Xeon 8358 processor operating at 2.6 GHz. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled, delivering 16 vCPUs alongside 32.0 GB of system memory. This resource profile yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual processor, targeting environments where processing density takes priority over massive memory allocations. The instance does not bundle integrated local storage, requiring attached block volumes for persistent data, nor does it include GPU accelerators. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned for connectivity. By avoiding surplus RAM and unneeded local disks, this setup delivers balanced hardware efficiency for dedicated compute tasks. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.8-32 is suited for microservices hosting, CI/CD runners, batch compute routines, and web serving.
